q4.7:
Farming is subject to "production" metrics and treated like a "factory"
Many of the "climate" issues and human disease issues can be solved by eliminating the pesticides, artificial fertilisers, GM seeds etc.
Nature is our blueprint and template for sustainable food production.  The "old" ways of farming e.g. rotating crops, working with the seasons and allowing natural pests to exterminate weeds etc takes time but it works
The soil is weakened and depleted by the external application of slurry, artificial fertilisers etc
Removal of trees and hedges to allow huge mass production machinery to easily manoeuvre has created vast deserts of farm fields allowing the rich topsoil to be blown or washed away and creating compacted surfaces which repel water means drought conditions happen faster.
Inadequate water systems capturing rain water in winter for use during dryer months.
The compacted soil just floods in winter and doesn't enable the earth to maintain moisture
Similarly the removal of trees and hedges provides no shelter for animals or shade for hedgerow plant and animal diversity
The pesticide companies, artificial fertiliser companies etc need to stop interfering in the natural cycles ✋️ 
They need to start understanding nature and supporting the earth to return to.the sustainable blueprint we had before industrial food production
Education at every level - local food cooperative - people buying from farm shops - "big food" banned from making farmers plough whole harvests into the ground because of their greed
The whole end to end system requires radical change
Farmers need support - not scorn
Farmers need gratitude- not family farm taxes
People need to reconnect to the earth and what they eat - understand the source and be encouraged to grow their own too.

I think that it is still more profitable to farm in an environmentally damaging way. As well as incentivising farmers to implement nature-based solutions, the government should raise revenues by taxing environmentally damaging facets of agriculture eg red diesel, artificial fertiliser, pesticides, fungicides and herbicides. 

I also think that the agricultural colleges are not doing enough to teach agro-ecological approaches to agriculture.

I think it needs really good people at a local level to make anything actually happen on the ground on a landscape level. It takes a lot of effort and persuasion, even if there is a financial carrot. The other point is trust in the government. Farming is a long term game, but governments and funding schemes are not. This needs to be resolved.
